message.content:
Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became fascinated by mortal settlements when they set foot in a city.
They loved the nicely paved ground and the intricate bridges that crossed the rivers.
Most of all, they loved houses with warm hearths and open doors.
Stone walls forming shelters from the weather yet connected the earth with the stories from every family.
They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self made staff.
Pebble Spring watched the masons shape each block with patient hands.
Pebble Spring noticed how moss softened the edges of the newest walls.
Pebble Spring carried a small branch and tested the wind near the chimney.
Pebble Spring found that fire needed air as much as it needed fuel.
Pebble Spring placed a leaf on the floor and listened to the rain outside.
Pebble Spring asked the village carpenter why the door frame leaned slightly east.
The carpenter smiled and said that the earth always shifted under stone.
Pebble Spring understood that a house was alive in many quiet ways.
Pebble Spring marked the beams with bright knots and small white dots.
Pebble Spring sang a short song while the mortar dried in the evening air.
Pebble Spring learned to measure the roof so the rain would slide away cleanly.
Pebble Spring built a tiny window so the morning light could enter the room.
Pebble Spring painted the lintel with a pattern of vines and berries.
Pebble Spring placed a stone hearth in the center of the warm room.
Pebble Spring hung a lantern by the door and it glowed through the fog.
Pebble Spring watched the neighbors walk past and wave to the new builder.
Pebble Spring felt happy when the roof did not leak after the first storm.
Pebble Spring knew the cottage needed one last touch before the season changed.
The cheerful Leshy Pebble Spring decorated the stone floor with moss and tiny flowers while the wind kept the hearth fire alive in the old city under the quiet stars and the fire looked spotty now
